name: Schwarzschild radius r_s = 2GM/c^2; a region inside its own Schwarzschild radius is a black hole (collapse criterion 2GM/c^2 >= l for a uniform ball)

published_statement: Schwarzschild 1916 interior (physics/9912033): the line element inside a homogeneous incompressible sphere is eq.(35) ds^2 = ((3 cos chi_a - cos chi)/2)^2 dt^2 - (3/kappa rho0)[dchi^2 + sin^2 chi dOmega^2], with rho0 + p = rho0 2 cos chi_a/(3 cos chi_a - cos chi) (eq.30); 'the radius measured outside' P_o = sqrt(3/kappa rho0) sin chi_a is 'identical with the value R_a' of the exterior areal coordinate (eq.39); 'alpha/P_o = sin^2 chi_a, alpha = (kappa rho0/3) P_o^3' (eq.40); 'For large distances the motion of the point occurs according to Newton's law, with alpha/2k^2 playing the role of the attracting mass'; 'At the center of the sphere velocity of light and pressure become infinite when cos chi_a = 1/3, and the fall velocity becomes sqrt(8/9) of the velocity of light. Hence there is a limit to the concentration, above which a sphere of incompressible fluid can not exist'; 'a sphere of given gravitational mass alpha/2k^2 can not have a radius measured from outside smaller than P_o = alpha. For a sphere of incompressible fluid the limit will be 9/8 alpha. (For the Sun alpha is equal to 3 km, for a mass of 1 gram is equal to 1.5 . 10^-28 cm.)' Hayward (gr-qc/9408002 p.4-5), with E = (r/2)(1 - g^{-1}(dr,dr)): 'Proposition 1: trapping. A metric sphere is trapped if and only if E > r/2, marginal if and only if E = r/2, and untrapped if and only if E < r/2. Proof. By definition.' -- 'physically important because it shows that the ratio E/r controls the formation of black and white holes, and trapped spheres generally'; future (past) outer trapping horizons 'will be taken as the definition of black (respectively white) holes'. Textbook form the tree uses: r_s = 2GM/c^2; a uniform ball of areal radius l and energy density u has M = u (4/3) pi l^3 / c^2, and is (marginally) trapped iff 2GM/c^2 >= l.
published_hypotheses: classical GR, Einstein's field equations without cosmological constant (1916: kappa = 8 pi k^2; Hayward eq.10-11 for dE/dr = 4 pi r^2 rho)
spherical symmetry (1916 Sec.3 'rotation symmetry around the origin'; Hayward: 'assumed implicitly in the Propositions')

1916 interior: STATIC equilibrium (eq.6), isotropic perfect fluid of CONSTANT density rho0 (eq.2, 'incompressible'), regular centre (eta = 0 at x = 0; lambda = 0 fixed by 'pressure at the center finite and positive'), p = 0 and C^1 matching to the exterior at the surface
the radius in the criterion is the AREAL radius ('radius measured outside', P_o = circumference/2 pi), not the proper radius P_i = sqrt(3/kappa rho0) chi_a
the mass in the criterion is the gravitational (Schwarzschild / Misner-Sharp) mass alpha/2k^2, not the 'substantial mass' rho0 V over proper volume (eq.41, 43: they differ)
Hayward Prop.1 is a statement about TRAPPING of a metric sphere (future OR past), not about black holes; 'black hole' = future outer trapping horizon, 'white hole' = past

trapped => singularity / black hole needs further hypotheses not in either source: Penrose 1965 (null energy condition, non-compact Cauchy surface, global hyperbolicity) and weak cosmic censorship for an event horizon (NAMED-NOT-READ)
hypothesis_drift: WEAKENED-TO-FALSE CONVERSE, not load-bearing -- specthm.py:612-613 H_collapse 'a region is a black hole IFF 2GM/c^2 >= l for that ball'. Neither source says iff-black-hole; Hayward's iff is for TRAPPED. Computed here both ways (rederive R5, closed-FRW dust = Oppenheimer-Snyder interior): (a) a sphere at chi = 0.02 lying inside the event horizon has 2m/R = 0.0024 < 1; (b) the time-reversed ball has 2m/R = 2.21 > 1 at its surface while expanding (a past-trapped, white-hole sphere, in no black hole). The tree uses only the forward direction (seat => 2GM/c^2 >= l), and spec.py:215 and specthm.py:1343 state the non-collapse side correctly as a NECESSARY condition ('avoiding collapse needs u < ...'), so this is an over-statement in a hypothesis label, not a refutation of SR2.

DROPPED -- 'black hole' vs 'trapped': spec.py:46-47 'it describes a black hole, by a factor of 6.58, always'; specthm.py:1837 z3 Implies(ball, bh). The source result delivers a trapped sphere; that it is a BLACK hole needs (i) future-trapped (collapsing, not expanding) and (ii) Penrose + cosmic censorship. What the tree's verdict actually needs -- that no STATIC device region exists -- is PROVED here with no extra hypothesis (R4, z3 unsat): 1 - 2m/R = Gamma^2 - U^2, so 2m/R = 2 pi^2/3 forces |dR/dtau| >= 2.362 c; the region is collapsing or exploding, never static.

Using it, u_seat/u_static-max = 3 pi^2/4 = 7.402 (R6d) -- a stricter bound, so the tree's refusal holds a fortiori on that hypothesis class.

lacked_data: M's hypothesis tested for this result. What the 1916 author had: the field equations and Newton's limit; no horizon interpretation (Lemaitre 1933, Finkelstein 1958), no trapped-surface concept (Penrose 1965), no quasi-local mass (Misner-Sharp 1964), no collapse solution (Oppenheimer-Snyder 1939), no observed black hole. Everything that came later is THEORY, and it changed the WORDING, not the number: the collapse criterion in the form the tree uses is a dimensionless statement 2Gm/(c^2 R) >= 1 in which no measured datum enters (sympy R1c: the ratio 2 pi^2/3 has no free symbols; G and c cancel). Later work sharpened it in two directions, both computed here: (i) the criterion is a TRAPPING criterion (Hayward Prop.1), trapped spheres may be past-trapped (white holes, R5b), and black-hole formation needs Penrose's hypotheses plus censorship -- this narrows the tree's 'is a black hole' to 'is trapped, hence not static' (R4), which is all the tree's verdict needs; (ii) the stricter static bound 8/9 was ALREADY in the 1916 paper ('the limit will be 9/8 alpha') and strengthens the tree's refusal to 3 pi^2/4 (R6d). Observational data since (LIGO 2015, EHT 2019 -- NAMED-NOT-READ) test the exterior geometry, not this criterion, and nothing in them is in tension with it. Evidence either way: no datum the author lacked moves the conclusion; the only things that move it are the tree's own DEFINING choices (ball radius = Sturm length, T_kk = u), R6.
grade_evidence: The external result STANDS as published and is re-derived: r_s = 2GM/c^2; Schwarzschild's 1916 uniform ball has gravitational mass exactly (4 pi/3) rho0 R^3 in the areal radius (R2c, eq.40), so the tree's M = u (4/3) pi l^3/c^2 is exact for areal l; a sphere is trapped iff 2Gm/(c^2 R) > 1 (Hayward Prop.1, READ; identity verified R4c); the tree's ratio 2 pi^2/3 = 6.5797 is exact and matches spec.seat_over_collapse to 1e-12 at four scales (R1, R7); no datum moves it. It is NARROWED because the tree uses it on a larger class, and with a stronger conclusion, than it holds on: (1) specthm.py:612-613 states 'black hole IFF 2GM/c^2 >= l'; the iff is false both ways, shown by computation (R5: an untrapped sphere inside an event horizon; an expanding past-trapped sphere) -- the converse is not load-bearing; (2) spec.py:46-47 / specthm.py:1837 conclude 'black hole' where the result gives 'trapped'; black hole additionally needs future-trapping plus Penrose + censorship (NAMED-NOT-READ). What IS proved without them (R4, z3) is that the region cannot be static (|dR/dtau| >= 2.362 c), which is what SR2's 'a device, not a black hole' needs; (3) l must be the areal radius and M the Misner-Sharp mass, unstated at spec.py:39-41 where l is the Sturm length; (4) spec.py:39 'ANY STURM-SEATING REGION' and spec.py:47 'always' exceed the tree's own H_ball: a radius-l/2 ball holding the seating chord with T_kk = 2u gives 2m/R = pi^2/12 = 0.82, not trapped (R6b, flat-chord approximation); (5) spherical only -- off spherical symmetry it is the unproven hoop conjecture (Dain 1401.8166), which the tree already routes to S-3. None of these is a refutation of SR2 on its stated hypotheses (ball of radius l): there every material row is trapped (min 3.29, R6a) and Schwarzschild's own 9/8 bound makes it stricter (3 pi^2/4 = 7.40, R6d). Source caveat: live alphaXiv and arXiv were unavailable this stage; the sources were READ from full texts cached in the scratchpad from earlier alphaXiv results.
what_would_change_the_grade: To STANDS: the tree restating H_collapse as the one-directional trapping criterion ('if 2Gm/c^2 >= l for the areal radius l then the sphere is trapped, hence the region is not static'), l named as the areal radius, and spec.py:39/47's 'ANY'/'always' restricted to H_ball (or the l/2-ball and T_kk/u cases computed and shown trapped). To WRONG: only a regular, spherically symmetric, static (or future-untrapped) configuration with 2Gm/(c^2 R) >= 1 in areal R -- impossible by R4 -- or a flaw in the ratio arithmetic, which R1/R7 reproduce exactly. To OPEN: nothing here; every piece is either read or computed. Reading Penrose 1965 and a censorship result at source would upgrade the 'trapped => black hole' step from NAMED to READ without moving the grade.
